summary.text: A male patient presented to the emergency department with left ankle pain and swelling after a twisting injury while playing football, with no significant medical history or ongoing treatments. Examination showed moderate swelling and deformity, soft compartments and no distal neurovascular deficits. A radiograph confirmed a bimalleolar fracture of the left ankle. A below-knee back-slab was applied, the orthopedic team reviewed the case, and open reduction and internal fixation was decided.

Preoperative assessment found the patient in good health, ASA 1E, 70 kg and 170 cm, with normal laboratory tests. Spinal anesthesia used hyperbaric bupivacaine 0.5% 3 mL with fentanyl 15 μg in the sitting position, with Ringer’s lactate co-loading. The block level was T8. Intravenous dexmedetomidine was started after block onset at 0.2 μg/kg/h without a loading dose and maintained during surgery.

About 90 minutes into the procedure, with the tourniquet inflated, the patient had sudden severe bradycardia with a heart rate of 20 beats/min, hypotension, a reduced conscious level and a peri-arrest situation. Airway remained patent, SpO2 was 97% and ECG showed sinus bradycardia. Intravenous atropine 0.5 mg was given and dexmedetomidine stopped; surgery was halted, and a second atropine dose with ephedrine 9 mg, plasma protein fraction and more oxygen followed.

Heart rate and blood pressure improved to 70 beats/min and 107/55 mm Hg, and epinephrine was not necessitated. Surgery resumed and was completed without further incident. The tourniquet was released after a total inflation time of 81 minutes and the surgical duration was 120 minutes. The patient was transferred to the postoperative care unit before being discharged to the ward.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract gives the age as 33 years and the case presentation gives 32 years.

evidence.quote: We report a 33-year-old male
A 32-year-old male presented

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not choose either age or average them; both are quarantined as a source conflict.

ambiguities.issue: The discussion says the 70/42 mm Hg blood pressure did not coincide with the moment of acute bradycardia (heart rate 20), although Table 2 lists it under "During arrhythmia".

evidence.quote: there was a discrepancy between the heart rate of 20 bpm and the blood pressure reading of 70/42 mm Hg, as the blood pressure measurement did not coincide with the moment of acute bradycardia

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not state that the blood pressure at the moment of heart rate 20 beats/min was 70/42 mm Hg or that it was measured at any particular time within the event.

ambiguities.issue: One sentence says the patient remained hemodynamically stable for the remainder of the procedure, but sudden bradycardia and hypotension are reported later during the same procedure.

evidence.quote: remained hemodynamically stable for the remainder of the procedure
Approximately 90 minutes into the procedure, with the tourniquet inflated, the patient experienced sudden bradycardia

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide until when the patient was stable or treat the stability statement as covering the event.

ambiguities.issue: The authors call the event a peri-arrest situation, pericardiac arrest, peri-cardiac arrest and bradyarrhythmia leading to pericardiac arrest.

evidence.quote: leading to a peri-arrest situation
bradyarrhythmia leading to pericardiac arrest
the risk of peri-cardiac arrest persists even in healthy young patients

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not state that cardiac arrest, loss of circulation or cardiopulmonary resuscitation occurred.

ambiguities.issue: High spinal and a vasovagal response to tourniquet pain are discussed as possible explanations and judged less likely or unlikely.

evidence.quote: it is less likely to have occurred in our patient
However, in our case, this scenario was deemed unlikely

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record either as present or as ruled out.

ambiguities.issue: The title and conclusion present the event as a serious adverse effect of low-dose dexmedetomidine, while the discussion also weighs other explanations.

evidence.quote: Our case exemplifies that this risk persists even in healthy young patients, at low drug infusion rates, and even after avoiding a loading dose
Also, severe tourniquet pain triggering a vasovagal response could be considered as a potential explanation for the event

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a confirmed causal link between dexmedetomidine and the event.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says intravenous atropine and ephedrine without saying whether intravenous applies to ephedrine.

evidence.quote: He was successfully revived with intravenous atropine and ephedrine

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a route to ephedrine.

ambiguities.issue: The block level is reported once after injection and once as assessed promptly after the patient stabilized, without saying whether these are the same assessment.

evidence.quote: The upper dermatomal level of block was noted to be T8
The level of the block was assessed promptly after the patient stabilized, revealing a T8 level

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge the two assessments or place the second before the dexmedetomidine infusion.

ambiguities.issue: The pre-operative baseline heart rate called normal in the discussion is not stated to be the Table 2 baseline heart rate of 78.

evidence.quote: his pre-operative baseline heart rate was within normal range
Baseline [rowspan=2,colspan=1] | HR | 78

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not flag the Table 2 value as normal or give the discussion statement a numeric value.

ambiguities.issue: A similar procedure on the medial malleolus is described only as using wire fixation; which steps were similar is not stated.

evidence.quote: A similar procedure was performed on the medial malleolus, utilizing wire fixation

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not add an incision, dissection or reduction on the medial malleolus.

ambiguities.issue: The authors suggest the patient's physically active status may have predisposed him to bradycardia through high vagal tone.

evidence.quote: may have also predisposed him to bradycardia due to high vagal tone

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record high vagal tone as present or as the cause of the bradycardia.

article_limitations: The article has no figures and no supplements, so no visual or supplement review applies.
Age is 33 years in the abstract and 32 years in the case presentation; both are review_only source-conflict facts.
Table 2 labels the 70/42 mm Hg blood pressure as during the arrhythmia, but the discussion says that reading did not coincide with the moment of acute bradycardia.
The case text says the patient remained hemodynamically stable for the remainder of the procedure before describing intraoperative bradycardia and hypotension.
Terminology for the event varies (peri-arrest, pericardiac arrest, peri-cardiac arrest); no loss of circulation or resuscitation is described.
Causality between dexmedetomidine and the event is asserted by the title and conclusion while other explanations are discussed; it is recorded only as a possible adverse effect (review_only).
Discussion statements about other published patients and guideline dosing are background and not recorded as facts of this patient.
